name: task_status
description: Inspect active and queued tasks visible in this conversation, including their IDs. Use before selecting a task if needed.
examples: what are you working on?
show my queued tasks

name: control_task
description: Actually stop, cancel, pause or resume work. Omit id and target for the active task. Use target to select by description (e.g. beehive); ambiguous matches return clarification. Only report the returned result. Never queue cancellation as gameplay work.

target.description: Words identifying an existing task; not a new task description.

examples: cancel the beehive task
I want you to stop what you're doing
put that task on hold

name: queue_task
description: Use this native function to actually queue an explicit request for Minecraft work; describing work in a reply does not queue it. Preserve requested counts, materials and coordinates. Include the actual requesting username. Work is attempted later, not performed immediately by this tool. New foreground work stops the same player's existing follow/stay mode by default; use resume_following only when explicitly requested.

resume_following.description: Set true only if the player explicitly asks to resume their previous following/staying mode after this work. Otherwise the new foreground request supersedes their old mode.

examples: come here and wait for a pickaxe
mine sixteen coal

name: search_memory
description: Look up scoped world memory. Return evidence, dimension and freshness; old sightings are not current observations.
examples: where did we build the house?

name: remember_location
description: Save the requesting player's CURRENT location using captured/loaded coordinates, never invented numbers or the bot's position. Any natural wording can select this tool. An optional name labels the place; otherwise use a player-specific default. It returns the saved coordinates or an error.
examples: can you remember the location I am currently at?
keep a note of this spot for me

name: update_memory
description: Remember, correct, rename or forget a world fact following the player's request. For CURRENT player coordinates use remember_location instead. Editing requires an existing record ID from search_memory. Coordinates must be supplied by the player or grounded in a referenced record.
examples: remember that I prefer spruce
forget the old home location

name: resolve_target
description: Resolve a concrete world reference: me/here, behind me, a block I am looking at, beside that chest, an explicit coordinate/entity, or a remembered landmark. Returns resolved, ambiguous or unresolved with an explanation. Does not move or edit blocks. Private memory is scoped automatically; cross-dimension and stale locations are rejected.

name.description: Player username, landmark name, or entity type. Omit player name for the requester.

examples: which block am I looking at?
where is the spot behind me?

name: set_movement
description: Start continuous following or staying under the task controller, or stop/resume the requester's previous following mode. Modes persist until stopped or lost. A new foreground request from the same player supersedes their mode by default; other players' work temporarily yields it. Explicitly requested resume_following on the new work preserves it for afterward. For follow, reference defaults to the requesting player; for stay, reference defaults to the bot's current position. For stay HERE use current_location. Query resolve_target for ambiguous world references. Do not claim movement finished: inspect the returned Started/Queued/error receipt. For an explicit new work request that needs clarification, use mode=prepare_work and question to stop the requester's old movement before asking. If the task is ready, call queue_task/create_project instead; they perform the handoff automatically.

name.description: Player username, landmark name, or entity type. Omit player name for the requester.

question.description: For prepare_work: ask the missing work details. The controller stops only this requester's follow/stay mode before delivering this clarification; no new work is queued.

examples: follow me at 3 blocks
stay here
stop following me
resume following
stay at home
stop following while we decide the house dimensions

name: create_project
description: Save a named, durable blueprint and normally queue construction. Ask for missing location/size/materials first. Cells are integer offsets relative to origin; specify ALL affected cells (1-4096 within 64x64 horizontal bounds). Actions default to place; remove/replace require expected original names AND explicit player permission for those exact changes. Never clear surrounding structures. Single-cell blocks only (no doors, beds or tall plants). Supported states: axis, single slab type top/bottom, furnace/chest facing. dependsOn lists relative positions of supports/earlier cells. execute=false is for requests to plan without building. New foreground work stops the same player's existing follow/stay mode by default; use resume_following only when explicitly requested.

name.description: Player username, landmark name, or entity type. Omit player name for the requester.

resume_following.description: Set true only if the player explicitly asks to resume their previous following/staying mode after this work. Otherwise the new foreground request supersedes their old mode.

examples: build and remember a project named garden wall
plan a small stone hut here without building it yet

name: revise_project
description: Save a new version of an existing project from an explicit revision request. Supply the full revised blueprint with relative offsets. Pause active construction and let the current operation settle before revising. Unchanged verified cells retain their receipts; changed cells require rechecking. A revision never automatically removes retired cells. To repair a conflicting player edit, explicitly specify replace and its expected block.

name.description: Player username, landmark name, or entity type. Omit player name for the requester.

examples: change the paused garden wall blueprint to use oak logs

name: continue_project
description: Continue an existing named project from saved blueprint and verified progress. Reconcile the world first; changed cells produce conflicts and are preserved. Queue execution; do not say building is already finished. New foreground work stops the same player's existing follow/stay mode by default; use resume_following only when explicitly requested.

resume_following.description: Set true only if the player explicitly asks to resume their previous following/staying mode after this work. Otherwise the new foreground request supersedes their old mode.

examples: continue the house

name: project_status
description: Read a scoped project by ID/name, or list visible projects if identifier is omitted. Reports version, bounds, verified/last-seen progress, missing resources and conflicts. Unknown chunks do not establish that a build is intact.
examples: what materials are missing for the house?
show my building projects

name: project_supplies
description: Queue a bounded material subtask (up to 64 of each item, 128 items total), then continue the project only if that subtask succeeds. Optionally use an explicitly authorized storage reference; otherwise gather/craft. Respect ownership and access notes. Uses existing/learned item workflows; no new Phase 4 container guarantees. New foreground work stops the same player's existing follow/stay mode by default; use resume_following only when explicitly requested.

name.description: Player username, landmark name, or entity type. Omit player name for the requester.

resume_following.description: Set true only if the player explicitly asks to resume their previous following/staying mode after this work. Otherwise the new foreground request supersedes their old mode.

examples: gather the next batch of missing materials for the house
use our materials chest to restock the wall project
